newsitem.title: UK: Booker to take '96 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Booker to take '96 restructuring charge.

text.p: British food distributor Booker Plc said on Friday it would take a restructuring charge of about 25 million stg against its 1996 results.
The company also said group sales for the year to December 28 rose three percent on a like-for-like basis and six percent overall compared with the previous year.
Booker said it would rationalise its network of Foodservice sites due to opportunities to utilise space at some of its recently-acquired Nurdin & Peacock Plc depots.
The company said it was making good progress on the integration of Nurdin & Peacock's cash-and-carry business, which it bought in November.

"While N&P's sales over the Christmas period were six percent lower than the previous year, its profit contribution in the period since the acquisition has been slightly higher than expected as a result of an improved product mix," Booker said in a statement.
At its other divisions, sales over the Christmas period were slightly ahead of last year, the company said.
Booker's shares closed at 399p on Thursday.
